output.title: Tool use before automation: pick one workflow first
output.body:
If you have tried ChatGPT but have not tied it to a real workflow yet, the first question is not “which AI tool?” It is “which repeatable job should we connect first?” Pick one workflow that happens every week and has a clear output: customer replies, invoice data entry, lead qualification, or something similar. Then map it on paper before you automate anything.

Write down three things: what enters the workflow, where the manual steps happen, and what decision rule is being used. If the work depends on your judgment, or your approval is the control gate, say that plainly. That is not a failure; it is the boundary. Human approval stays in place for money movement and other high-risk decisions.

For many small businesses, the practical choice is simple: improve the tool stack first, or add AI on top. If your email, CRM, documents, and SaaS tools are still disconnected, tool integration is usually the cheaper thing to test first. AI fits best where the work is repeatable and rule-based, not where every case needs a fresh judgment.

So the next step is to choose one workflow, document the handoffs, and mark the approval point. If the process is still mostly manual after that, you have a bounded problem worth fixing. If the process is already well connected, AI may have a sensible place. The tricky part is usually not the model; it is the plumbing.
